CLINICAL ENCOUNTER NOTE - SPINE CLINIC
Patient: Robert Johnson | Age: 52 | Sex: Male
Date of Service: 2024-03-12

SUBJECTIVE:
Pt is a 52yo M with persistent low back pain radiating down the left leg into the lateral calf and great toe for 10 weeks.
Pain is sharp, burning, 8/10 severity. Has completed 8 weeks of formal physical therapy with no relief. Also took meloxicam 15mg daily for 6 weeks with minimal benefit.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Lumbar Spine: Tenderness at L4-L5 interspace. Decreased sensation along left L5 dermatome. Positive straight leg raise on the left at 40 degrees. Lower extremity motor strength 4/5 left extensor hallucis longus.
No saddle anesthesia. Normal rectal tone.

ASSESSMENT & PLAN:
Left L5 radiculopathy secondary to suspected herniated nucleus pulposus. Failed conservative therapy > 6 weeks. Order Lumbar spine MRI without contrast (CPT 72148).

Patient: James Smith | Age: 35 | Sex: Female

PLAN: Right knee arthroscopy with partial medial meniscectomy (CPT 29881).
